newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Central Bank auctions CDs, yields fall.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Central Bank auctions CDs, yields fall.

text.p: Yields fell on Jordanian Certificates of Deposits (CDs) on Thursday for the first time in a year-and-a half after the central bank introduced competitive CD auctions, the bank said.

The average yield of the first competitive 50 million dinar ($70.5 million) bi-monthly CD auction which closed on Wednesday fell to 8.825 percent from a previously fixed 9.25 percent while the six-month paper also dropped to 9.033 percent from 9.50 percent.
Yields have remained fixed since January 1996 when they rose from 8.75 percent for three-month paper and 9.00 percent for six-months.
The yield offers accepted varied on three-month paper from a 8.90 percent high to a 8.750 percent low while six-month CDs yields ranged from a high of 9.10 percent to 9.000 percent.

The bi-monthly CD issue was covered 2.8 times with a total of bids received worth 139.8 million dinars of which 74.5 million dinars were for three-month paper and the remaining 65.3 million bids offered for six-month paper.
The Central Bank sold 35 million dinars worth of three-month CDs and 15 million dinars of six month CDs.

The competitive market dictated CD auction system enable yields to move more in line with supply and demand, but monetary authorities will have at their disposal a number of tools to inject or drain liquidity to ensure that interest rates do not steer away from the the target band, officials said.
The Central Bank keeps a high interest rate policy to make dinar-denominated assets attractive and prevent a flow of dinars into dollar-denominated assets.
